input: I need a shaft to transmit 5 kW at 300 rpm.
raw_text:
{
  "clarifying_questions": [
    "What is the expected duty cycle (continuous vs. intermittent) and any shock/impact loading?",
    "Is there a preferred keyway, spline, or coupling type at the shaft ends?",
    "What is the expected shaft length and bearing support span (for deflection/bending checks)?",
    "Are there any radial or axial loads from gears, pulleys, or sprockets mounted on the shaft?",
    "What is the operating environment (temperature, corrosion exposure, lubrication)?",
    "Is there a target fatigue life or safety factor required by the application standard?"
  ],
  "engineering_reasoning": "Torque was calculated from the given power and speed using T = P / omega. A solid circular shaft was sized against an allowable shear stress for a common medium-carbon steel, applying a standard service factor to account for typical torsional and minor bending loads in a general-purpose drive. This is a preliminary torsion-only sizing; actual diameter may need to increase once bending loads from mounted components (gears, pulleys, sprockets) and fatigue considerations are included.",
  "preliminary_calculations": {
    "power_kw": 5,
    "speed_rpm": 300,
    "angular_velocity_rad_s": 31.42,
    "torque_nm": 159.15,
    "shaft_diameter_mm": 25,
    "material_grade": "AISI 1045",
    "allowable_shear_stress_mpa": 42,
    "service_factor": 1.5,
    "design_torque_nm": 238.7
  },
  "material_suggestions": [
    "AISI 1045 medium-carbon steel (cost-effective, good machinability)",
    "AISI 4140 alloy steel (higher strength if duty cycle proves severe or shock loads present)",
    "AISI 304/316 stainless steel (if corrosion resistance is required)"
  ],
  "manufacturing_suggestions": [
    "Turn from round bar stock on a lathe",
    "Add a keyway via broaching or end milling for coupling/pulley attachment",
    "Grind shaft journals at bearing seats for tight tolerance and surface finish",
    "Consider induction hardening at bearing/seal contact areas for wear resistance"
  ],
  "recommended_next_steps": [
    "Confirm duty cycle, shock loading, and required fatigue/safety factor",
    "Determine shaft length, bearing locations, and any overhung loads",
    "Select a specific bearing and coupling to finalize shaft-end geometry",
    "Perform a combined bending-torsion fatigue check (e.g., ASME shaft design code) once loads are known",
    "Check deflection and critical speed if shaft length or overhung loads are significant"
  ]
}
